01 · Council places a special tax

Two-thirds
of voters.

Money earmarked for named purposes. This is what the 2026 motion proposed, and the hardest bar to clear.

  • $4 per square foot, every year
  • Streets, film retention, homebuyers
  • Up to $250 million a year, cited
Riviera · 168 ac · for-profit, not covered
02 · Council places a general tax

Simple
majority.

Money goes to the general fund with no earmark, on a regular election for Council seats. The next one is in 2028.

  • No earmark
  • Regular Council election
  • Next chance: 2028
Wilshire Blvd through Westwood · from the air
03 · Citizens put it on the ballot

Like
Measure ULA.

Voters gather signatures and qualify an initiative. A citizen-initiated special tax passes with a simple majority.

  • Signatures, not a Council vote
  • Simple majority
  • ULA passed with 58 percent
Rancho Park · the city’s public course
